item.title: Bear baiting in England became more common following Norman invasion, research reveals
item.description: Bear baiting in England became more popular after the Norman Conquest in 1066, new research shows. The study by Cardiff University and the University of Nottingham brings together archaeological analysis of bear bones and archival records to show the prevalence of the animals in England and northern France during medieval times. The study is published in the journal Society & Animals. Fuente: Phys.org.

La Administración Trump califica a estas personas de 'terroristas' sin aportar prueba alguna que certifique dichas actividades ilícitas. item.title: Male beauty ratings reveal lower averages but an exceptional upper tier
item.description: Women's faces are rated as more attractive than men's across cultures, age groups and sexual orientations. This effect, known as the "Gender Attractiveness Gap" (GAP), was recently demonstrated in a large-scale study led by the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics (MPIEA) in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. A new article in Current Opinion in Psychology takes a closer look at the underlying data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border , in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine. The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast. item.title: Heat waves inhibit antibiotic resistance in soils, but at a price
item.description: Extreme heat waves disrupt life in soil. Soil bacteria that produce and resist antibiotics switch into survival mode, temporarily reducing the number of resistance genes. At the same time, heat and drought are causing significant damage to soils and ecosystems, especially in cold, wet regions such as the Netherlands. This is evident from a large-scale European study by soil ecologist Franciska de Vries (University of Amsterdam) and colleagues. The findings are published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nuevo mapamundi aprobado en la ONU: ¿por qué África se verá diferente?
item.description: Durante siglos, la proyección de Mercator ha dominado nuestra forma de visualizar el mundo, pero también ha distorsionado el tamaño relativo de los continentes. África es uno de los grandes ejemplos: su superficie aparece mucho menor de lo que realmente es frente a Europa y otras regiones del planeta. Un nuevo modelo cartográfico busca corregir estas proporciones y ofrecer una representación más fiel del tamaño de los territorios. ¿Qué cambia en nuestra visión del mundo cuando dejamos atrás el mapa tradicional? item.title: US war on Iran: 'Incompetent administration when it comes to negotiations and prosecuting war'
item.description: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Simpson Center. She frames the war in the Persian Gulf as a mutually damaging stalemate in which neither Washington nor Tehran has found a politically sustainable exit: "There are no winners in this war". Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: The year is 2060. London shudders through months of Nordic winter freezes. In U.S. coastal cities such as Miami and Charleston, South Carolina, sea levels have risen three feet (about 0.9 meters), with routine tidal flooding washing away streets. item.title: 12 nations announce trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank
item.description: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accused "settler terrorists" of "ethnic cleansing" in areas of the West Bank and said the UK was bringing in an "import ban on goods from illegal settlements." Israel closed the British consulate in Jerusalem in response. Publicado también por: The New York Times - World. Fuente: Euronews.
